newsitem.title: POLAND: Merrill Lynch advises Polish overweight stance.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch advises Polish overweight stance.

text.p: Merrill Lynch recommended investors to stay overweight in Polish equities, saying the market was still undervalued despite its more than 90-percent rise for the year so far.
"While investors are now having to pay twice what was paid for a stock a year ago, we believe the market to be still undervalued," Merrill Lynch said in its report dated September 25.
Poland still remained cheap in the global context, the report said.
It said Poland's long term growth prospects, based on a successful macroeconomic picture and accelerating foreign investment, provided an attractive investment opportunity.
Merrill Lynch said, however, a more selective approach was warranted, with focus on infrastructure and banking stocks, where it recommended building positions for the longer term.
It said it believed firms in those sectors were likely to outperform Poland's expected five-percent annual growth rate.
It recommended Agros, Polifarb Cieszyn and Elektrim as accumulate, forecasting their price-earnings ratio at 12.6, 12.8 and 18.6 in 1996 and 9.7, 9.6 and 14.5 in 1997, respectively.
Currectly Agros P/E ratio was at 16.9, Polifarb's at 16.5 and Elektrim's 23.6.
